To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have found a new meet-in-the-middle technique that is applicable to a large class of linear s-boxes and that this technique is very efficient when applied to LED-64.
we have improved the complexity of the best known attacks against 1, 2, and 3-step LED64 in the single-key model from \(2^{64}\), \(2^{60.5}\) to \(2^{60},2^{48}\), respectively.
we have found a new technique to speed up MITM attacks, which is based on the use of linear sieving, and that we have used it to break 2-step LED and 3-step LED.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the efficiency of the linear sieving technique, a core component of MITM attacks.
the design of new linear sieving techniques for the purpose of finding large linear trails in the lightweight block cipher LBlock, which can be used to construct MITM attacks on LED-64.
the security of step-reduced LED-64 and provides a better understanding of the security of this lightweight block cipher.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our attacks on LED-64 are the best known attacks to date.
, with the exception of 2-step LED, our attacks are significantly faster than the previously known attacks.

the current state of knowledge on the security of LED-64 is that it can be attacked with complexity \(2^{49} \cdot 2^{16} \approx 2^{63}\) and time-memory trade-off of \(2^{63}\), and the attack can be extended to 4 rounds by using a related key model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the complexity of our attacks is at most \(2^{48.5}\) for the single-key model and at most \(2 ^{49.5}\) in the related-key model.
the MITM attacks on LED-64 are now as efficient as the best known differential attacks.

we have reduced the complexity of known-plaintext attacks on LED-64 from \(2^{60} \) to \(2^{49} \) in the single-key model, and from \(2^{120} \) to 2 ^{96} in the related-key model, and reduced the complexity of related-key attacks on LED- 64 from \(2^{{120}} \) to \( 2^{96} \) in single-key model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MITM technique can be very efficient when the linear layers in the cipher are simple, and the linear layers are not necessarily the bottleneck of the attack.

the meet-in-the-middle attacks on LED-64 can be improved by using the linear sieve technique, which was originally introduced by Bogdanov et al. (EUROCRYPT’14) and later applied to LED-64 in EUROCRYPT’15 by Wang et al. We
the MITM technique can be used to attack LED-64, and possibly other ciphers as well, even if they have large key sizes and large number of rounds.
